content: The Court of L'Aquila addressed a husband's claim for €110,034 in reimbursements for property improvements. The judge clarified that expenditures made during the marriage using marital income are not refundable upon division. Under Article 192 of the Civil Code, only funds proven to originate from a separate personal estate qualify. Since the husband failed to prove his salary was separate from the community, his claim was rejected. Another legal issue was the "marketability" of the property due to minor urban planning discrepancies. The court applied recent high court rulings stating that "textual nullity" only applies if the building permit is absent. Since a permit existed, the minor discrepancies did not block a future judicial sale. The final ruling ordered the property's sale since it was indivisible and no assignment was requested.
